classification.difficultyReason: Connects the angle sum in a spatial triangle with two vertical right triangles to determine height and depression.

content.prompt: Two monuments $A$ and $B$ are $400\text{ m}$ apart on the horizontal plane. The angle of depression of $A$ from the top $T$ of a tall building is $18^\circ$. $\angle TAB=52^\circ$ and $\angle TBA=38^\circ$.

spec.description: Building TC perpendicular to the ground plane, triangle TAB, dashed ground constructions and parallel horizontal depression reference. Source cyan angle fills are replaced by unfilled black angle marks.
spec.mathematics: AB=400 m; angle TAB=52 degrees; angle TBA=38 degrees; depression of A=18 degrees; TC=h.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens remain visible; no calculated answers are included.

answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}\angle ATB&=180^\circ-52^\circ-38^\circ\\&=90^\circ\end{aligned}$

Thus $AB$ is the hypotenuse of $\triangle ATB$.

$\begin{aligned}\cos52^\circ&=\frac{TA}{400}\\TA&=400\cos52^\circ\end{aligned}$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the height $h$ of the building, correct to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
The angle of elevation $\angle TAC$ equals the angle of depression, $18^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}\sin18^\circ&=\frac{h}{TA}\\h&=TA\sin18^\circ\\&=400\cos52^\circ\sin18^\circ\\&\approx76\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the angle of depression of $B$ from $T$, to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Let the angle of depression be $\beta$. It equals $\angle TBC$.

$\begin{aligned}TB&=400\sin52^\circ\\\sin\beta&=\frac{h}{TB}\\&=\frac{400\cos52^\circ\sin18^\circ}{400\sin52^\circ}\\\beta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos52^\circ\sin18^\circ}{\sin52^\circ}\right)\\&\approx14^\circ\end{aligned}$
